block: SQ2 (companion structured review, methods): estimators and identifying assumptions for a simultaneous policy shock with a continuous dose, misclassified treatment (false positives) and few control or treated clusters. Sub-topics (a) to (e). This is a PRESS 2015 peer review of the calibration, with 23 re-run OpenAlex calls through Firecrawl on 2026-10-12. One call failed with HTTP 400 because has_abstract is not a valid select field, and one hit a 429 rate limit and was retried. Firecrawl reported low credits, so the user should add credits before further runs.

press_items.assessment: The five sub-topics match the question, and the reviewer brief's pesticide synonyms (agrochemical, fungicide, procymidone, aerial application, drift and so on) were rightly left out: SQ2 is a methods block with no population restriction, and only arm (e) touches agriculture, through suitability and GM vocabulary. There are three gaps. (1) The question asks for identifying assumptions for a simultaneous shock, but no sub-topic covers pre-trend testing or parallel-trends sensitivity. Two examples are Rambachan & Roth 2023 (10.1093/restud/rdad018, indexed as T10845/2613) and Roth's pretest work. The project depends on exactly this: the SPT pre-trend test in 10_spt_pretrend.py, and three anticipation dates in 2015, 2018 and 2019. (2) Fuzzy or treatment-rate designs are non-binary DiD, the aggregate-dose analogue, and they were outside (a). (3) Circular validation. The reported recall (11/11 for a-d) was measured on the same seeds that shaped the strings. On an independent validation set it fell sharply for (b) and (c); see the tests below.
press_items.suggested_change: Add independent validation items that were not used for tuning, for every sub-topic. Optionally add an (f) arm for parallel-trends testing, sensitivity and anticipation, for example ("parallel trends" OR "pre-trends" OR "pretrends" OR "pre-trend") AND (test OR testing OR sensitivity OR "no anticipation" OR anticipation). The (f) arm was NOT tested here, so no count is claimed. Alternatively, record a protocol decision that this literature comes in by known-item and citation chasing.
press_items.tested: Validation DOIs first checked for indexing (call R1: 14/14 indexed). Note: the DOI I guessed for Mahajan 2006, 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00692.x, resolves to Pesaran 2006. The correct DOI is 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00677.x, found by title search (R3).

press_items.assessment: The AND/OR nesting is correct and the parsed oql trees confirm it. The structural flaw is that, with no proximity operator, the few-cluster concept (c) was captured only by contiguous phrases ('few clusters', 'small number of clusters'). The methods literature mostly writes 'when the number of clusters/groups is small' or 'small numbers of states'. The phrase 'few clusters' also does not match 'Few Heterogeneous Clusters'. In (b), the left context block required DiD or treatment-effect wording, which excludes the misclassified-binary-regressor econometrics (Bollinger 1996; Mahajan 2006) that Denteh-Kédagni build on. The right block covered misreporting only through the phrases 'treatment misreporting' and 'misreported treatment', so it missed 'treatment effects with endogenous misreporting'.
press_items.suggested_change: For (c), add a second OR arm: ("number of clusters" OR "number of groups" OR "number of states") AND ("difference in differences" OR "standard errors" OR "t-statistic" OR "cluster-robust"). Also add "heterogeneous clusters", "randomization tests", bare "cluster-robust" and "clustered standard errors" to the first arm. For (b), add "binary regressor", "treatment status", "treatment indicator" and "program participation" to the context block, and the single words misreporting and misreported to the error block. Also add a measurement-error arm keyed on binary regressor, treatment status and treatment indicator.
press_items.tested: R7: C_v2 (filtered) plus 7 canonical few-cluster papers not used in tuning (BDM 2004 QJE, Donald-Lang 2007, Ibragimov-Müller 2016, Canay-Romano-Shaikh 2017 Ecta, Pustejovsky-Tipton 2018, Imbens-Kolesár 2016, Cameron-Miller 2015 JHR) returned 1/7, only Cameron-Miller. R11: C_v3-lean returned 1,933 (C_v2: 1,025). R22: C_v3-lean on all 15 (c) items returned 14/15; it missed Imbens-Kolesár, whose abstract has only 'robust standard errors' and 'clusters'. R9/R10: C_v3-broad, which adds "robust standard errors", "permutation test(s)", "randomization test", "hypothesis testing" and "panel data", returned 2,400 with 15/15. R4: B_final (filtered) plus 6 misclassification items returned 1/6, only Lewbel 2007; it missed Nguimkeu-Denteh-Tchernis JoE 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.10.005, their NBER w24117, Mahajan 2006, Bollinger 1996 and Kreider et al. 2012. R5: B_v2 returned 447 (B_final: 323). R6: B_v2 on 8 items returned 7/8; the only miss was Kreider 2012, which the subfield filter drops.

press_items.assessment: OpenAlex has no thesaurus. The primary_topic.subfield filter (2002, 2613, 2000, 1804) plays that role and is the main precision lever. It is not neutral. Kreider, Pepper, Gundersen & Jolliffe 2012 (JASA, 'Identifying the effects of SNAP ... when participation is endogenous and misreported', 10.1080/01621459.2012.682828) is classified in subfield 3600 General Health Professions and is lost under every filtered string. The original calibration already showed the same risk for DRS, Reynier-Rubin and Costinot. JEL codes, the natural controlled vocabulary here (C21, C23, C12, C15), are not in OpenAlex, and EconLit was not available.
press_items.suggested_change: Run each filtered string a second time with topics.id:T10845 (any of a work's topics) in place of the subfield filter, and union the two runs by OpenAlex ID. One filter value cannot express subfield OR topic. That second run was not executed, so its added volume is unknown. Record in the protocol that health-services and political-methodology venues are covered only through the T10845 run and the arXiv/web supplements.
press_items.tested: R1 primary_topic lookup: Kreider 2012 is T11610, subfield 3600, so it is outside the filter. All other validation items checked are 2613 or 2002, so their failures come from the search strings, not the filter. Hsiao, Ching & Wan 2012 is T11911/2002.

press_items.assessment: Several key synonyms are missing. (a) fuzzy and "treatment rate": de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille 2018 'Fuzzy Differences-in-Differences' (10.1093/restud/rdx049) has neither 'continuous treatment' nor 'treatment intensity'. Also missing are "intensity of treatment", "continuously distributed", dosage, "exposure intensity", "continuous exposure", "changes in changes" and TWFE. (b) misreporting, misreported, "binary regressor", "treatment status", "treatment indicator". (c) The "number of clusters/groups/states" arm, "heterogeneous clusters", "randomization tests", bare "cluster-robust", "clustered standard errors", and optionally "robust standard errors" and "permutation test(s)". (d) estimation and "research design": Abadie 2021 JEL was missed because D2 lists 'estimator' and the abstract says 'estimation'/'estimates'. Also "single treated" in place of "single treated unit", and the factor-model and matrix-completion family: "panel data approach", "panel data method", "matrix completion" and "interactive fixed effects" AND (counterfactual(s) OR "program evaluation" OR "policy evaluation" OR "treatment effect(s)" OR "causal effect"). Hsiao-Ching-Wan 2012 (10.1002/jae.1230) never says 'synthetic control'. dCDH AER 2020 (10.1257/aer.20181169) and the dCDH 2023 survey (10.1093/ectj/utac017) have no dose vocabulary. They are binary-treatment heterogeneity papers, which CLAUDE.md classes as conceptual references, so missing them is acceptable if recorded as a scope decision. (e) was not re-tested. The citation-chasing arm is sound, but Adão-Kolesár-Morales 2019 (10.1093/qje/qjz025) should be added as a cites: anchor or a known item.
press_items.suggested_change: Adopt A2, B_v2, C_v3-lean (or C_v3-broad if volume allows) and D3 as given in recommended_final_query.
press_items.tested: R12: A1 (filtered) on 7 items returned 4/7. It missed Fuzzy DiD, dCDH AER 2020 and the dCDH survey; it retrieved D'Haultfoeuille-Hoderlein-Sasaki JoE 10.1016/j.jeconom.2022.07.003 on its title. R14: A2 returned 356 (A1: 240). R15: A2 on the same 7 returned 5/7 and now includes Fuzzy DiD. R16: D2 (filtered) on 8 SC/SDID items returned 6/8; it missed Abadie 2021 JEL and Hsiao et al. 2012. R18: D3 returned 1,244 (D2: 934). R19: D3 on the same 8 returned 8/8, adding Abadie 2021, Hsiao et al. 2012, Athey et al. 2021 matrix completion, Xu 2017 GSC, ADH 2010, ASCM, SDID and Chernozhukov-Wüthrich-Zhu.

press_items.assessment: (1) The calibration's syntax note overstates stemming. OpenAlex conflates inflections (estimator and estimators, test and tests), but D2's 'estimator' did not retrieve an abstract that contains 'estimation.' and 'estimates' (R16 and R17). Derivational variants therefore have to be listed one by one. Wildcards were not tested. (2) Phrases are contiguous: 'few clusters' does not match 'few heterogeneous clusters', and 'clustered errors' does not match 'clustered standard errors'. (3) Hyphens act as spaces, so the bare phrase "cluster-robust" covers 'cluster-robust variance estimation' and makes "cluster-robust inference" redundant. (4) Withheld abstracts. The J Econometrics record for DHS 2023 returns abstract_inverted_index null. Yet has_abstract is true for all 46,639 works whose primary topic is T10845 (R20), so whether withheld publisher abstracts are searchable is UNTESTED. Elsevier and JoE papers may be matched on their titles only. (5) The ordered query log is reproducible. The recall figures attached to the final strings should be relabelled as tuning recall, not validation recall.
press_items.suggested_change: Correct the stemming claim in syntax_findings. List derivational variants explicitly (estimator, estimators, estimation, estimate, estimates where relevant). Use known-item checks on JoE titles as a safeguard. Verify every validation DOI by an indexing call before running recall, because one guessed DOI here resolved to the wrong paper.
press_items.tested: R17: the Abadie 2021 abstract contains 'estimation.' and 'estimates' but D2 did not retrieve it. R13: DHS JoE abstract_inverted_index null. R20: group_by=has_abstract on primary_topic.id:T10845 gave true for all 46,639 records and false for 0. R2: has_abstract:false over the 21 seed and validation DOIs returned 0.

press_items.assessment: No date, language or type limits were used, which is right for methods. The year metadata drift (Conley-Taber 2010 vs 2011; Ferman-Pinto 2018 vs 2019) is documented. The subfield filter is the only limit and is discussed under subject headings. Volume trade-off after revision: (a) 356; (b) 447; (c) 1,933 lean or 2,400 broad; (d) 1,244. The revised a-d union in one call returns 3,840, against 2,416 before; the parts sum to 3,980, so about 140 records overlap. With the unchanged (e) arms (about 256) this comes to roughly 4,100 gross before version deduplication, against about 2,670 before. That is +55%, and most of the increase comes from (c). If volume is binding, two options keep 14/15 or more on the validation set: use C_v3-lean rather than broad, or use the T10845 topic restriction for (d) (not re-tested with D3).
press_items.suggested_change: Accept the increase. The original (b) and (c) strings missed 5 of 6 and 6 of 7 independent canonical papers, which a methods review cannot defend. Report per-arm counts and union counts in the PRISMA-S log, and deduplicate preprint, SSRN, NBER and journal versions before screening.
press_items.tested: R21: the revised union (A2 OR B_v2 OR C_v3-lean OR D3), filtered, returned 3,840. The per-arm counts are R5, R11, R14 and R18 above. The (e) arms and an unfiltered union were not re-run.

recommended_final_query:
OpenAlex, one call, filter=primary_topic.subfield.id:2002|2613|2000|1804,title_and_abstract.search:
(("difference in differences" OR "event study" OR "two-way fixed effects" OR "parallel trends" OR "changes in changes" OR TWFE) AND ("continuous treatment" OR "treatment intensity" OR "intensity of treatment" OR "dose-response" OR dosage OR "multi-valued treatment" OR "multivalued treatment" OR "non-binary treatment" OR "heterogeneous adoption" OR "treatment dose" OR stayers OR fuzzy OR "treatment rate" OR "continuously distributed" OR "exposure intensity" OR "continuous exposure"))
OR ((("difference in differences" OR "parallel trends" OR "event study" OR "treatment effect" OR "treatment effects" OR "causal effect" OR "policy evaluation" OR "program evaluation" OR "binary regressor" OR "treatment status" OR "treatment indicator" OR "program participation") AND (misclassification OR misclassified OR misreporting OR misreported OR "mismeasured treatment" OR "mismeasured binary" OR "measurement error in treatment" OR "treatment measurement error")) OR (("difference in differences" OR "parallel trends" OR "event study" OR "binary regressor" OR "treatment status" OR "treatment indicator") AND ("measurement error" OR "errors in variables" OR mismeasured OR mismeasurement)))
OR ((("few clusters" OR "few treated" OR "few control" OR "few untreated" OR "few groups" OR "small number of clusters" OR "small number of groups" OR "small number of treated" OR "small number of control" OR "small number of policy changes" OR "finite number of clusters" OR "single treated" OR "one treated" OR "unbalanced clusters" OR "clustered errors" OR "cluster bootstrap" OR "wild cluster bootstrap" OR "wild bootstrap" OR "randomization inference" OR "permutation inference" OR "conformal inference" OR "cluster-robust" OR "heterogeneous clusters" OR "randomization tests" OR "clustered standard errors") AND ("difference in differences" OR cluster OR clusters OR clustered OR "policy change" OR "policy changes" OR "few treated" OR "synthetic control")) OR (("number of clusters" OR "number of groups" OR "number of states") AND ("difference in differences" OR "standard errors" OR "t-statistic" OR "cluster-robust")))
OR ((("synthetic control" OR "synthetic controls" OR "synthetic difference in differences" OR "synthetic DiD") AND (inference OR estimator OR estimators OR estimation OR "few treated" OR "single treated" OR "small number" OR permutation OR placebo OR conformal OR "bias correction" OR identification OR "research design")) OR (("panel data approach" OR "panel data method" OR "matrix completion" OR "interactive fixed effects") AND (counterfactual OR counterfactuals OR "program evaluation" OR "policy evaluation" OR "treatment effect" OR "treatment effects" OR "causal effect")))
[Result: 3,840 on 2026-10-12. Validation recall: (a) 5/7, where the 2 misses are binary-TWFE papers that are out of scope by decision; (b) 7/8, where the miss is lost to the subfield filter; (c) 14/15; (d) 8/8.]
Optional broad (c): add "robust standard errors" OR "permutation test" OR "permutation tests" OR "randomization test" to the first (c) arm, and "hypothesis testing" OR "panel data" to the second. The (c) arm then returns 2,400 alone with 15/15.
Plus a second run of the same string with topics.id:T10845 in place of the subfield filter, unioned by ID (not executed; recovers off-subfield methods papers such as Kreider et al. 2012).
Plus the (e) arms unchanged from the calibration: E6 shift-share/formula instruments (topics.id:T10845, 108), the cites: arm on 5 GAEZ anchors with suitability vocabulary (119; add AKM 10.1093/qje/qjz025 as an anchor or known item), and the 29-hit GAEZ keyword arm.
Plus the arXiv research-index, Wiley and NBER/SSRN/RePEc supplements as calibrated.
missing_concepts_or_synonyms: "number of clusters" / "number of groups" / "number of states" (BDM 2004; Donald-Lang 2007; Pustejovsky-Tipton 2018)
parallel-trends pretesting and sensitivity (Rambachan-Roth 2023, 10.1093/restud/rdad018): no arm
anticipation / "no anticipation" (three anticipation dates in the project): no arm
pesticide/agrochemical synonyms from the reviewer brief: deliberately NOT applicable to this methods block
